To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) The D-brane vertex operator is the gauge theory vertex operator in the presence of external matter; 2) D-brane boundary states are the wavefunctionals of vacuum gauge theory with external matter; 3) D-brane tensions arise through dynamical mechanisms in a conformally-invariant three-dimensional scalar field theory; 4) D-brane states can be constructed from the gauge theory wavefunctional through string descendent states

the branes arise in the orbifold of the three-dimensional gauge and gravity theories through the orbifold relations and the induced worldsheet action, and that the brane tension arises through a conformally-invariant dynamical coupling to the scalar theory.

(i) the brane vertex operators naturally arise in induced worldsheet action, (ii) the boundary states are wavefunctionals of three-dimensional theory, (iii) the brane tension arises from dynamical mechanisms, (iv) string descendent states are described by excited wavefunctionals, and (v) the brane states satisfy Cardy condition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction and study of D-branes in three-dimensional topological theories.

the following question: How does one obtain the physics of branes in a theory which does not contain them as fundamental objects? In particular, what are the physical consequences of orbifolding a topologically massive theory in three dimensions?
the study of topological field theories, in particular topologically massive gauge theories and topological gravity, and their relation to string theory.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
D-branes are naturally described as vacuum wavefunctionals in three-dimensional gauge theories with orbifold boundary conditions.

we have shown how to construct a three-dimensional theory which is a natural generalisation of the two-dimensional string theory, in which brane vertex operators naturally emerge and in which branes are naturally described as boundary states.

the D-brane states in the three dimensions can be described as the vacuum wavefunctionals for the three-dimensional gauge and gravity theories, which are induced from the bulk theory by the orbifold relations, and which are minimally coupled to the matter fields in the bulk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown how D-branes arise naturally in three-dimensional theories with a topological gauge field.

we have given a concrete realisation of the brane states and their dynamics in a topologically massive three-dimensional theory, which is an example of the kind of theories that are of interest in the AdS/CFT correspondence, and we have shown how the brane tension arises dynamically from bulk interactions.

the D-brane states in topological membranes can be naturally described in terms of wavefunctionals of a three-dimensional gauge theory with a dynamical mass scale, and that these wavefunctions are compatible with the orbifold relations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the branes arise naturally in the theory, and their properties are a consequence of the underlying dynamics.
the brane tension in topological field theories can arise dynamically, and that brane vertex operators can arise naturally as the result of a consistent orbifold construction.

the orbifold construction of D-brane states in the topologically massive theories is a very natural one, and that the branes can be described by a worldsheet action that is conformally-invariant, and hence is free from the usual problems of topological membranes.
